title: What is Directed Studies?
text:
Directed Studies (DS) is a selective, year-long program for first-year students at Yale College. It is an interdisciplinary introduction to influential texts in the Western and Near Eastern traditions, from the ancient Mediterranean to the twentieth century.
The program consists of three integrated, full-year courses taken together:

Literature
Philosophy
Historical and Political Thought

Each course meets weekly for one lecture and two small seminars led by Yale faculty. Roughly ten percent of each first-year class is admitted. Students read heavily and write analytic essays throughout the year, and the essays in this section come from that work.
The fall term covers antiquity through the Middle Ages; the spring term runs from the Renaissance to the twentieth century.
Learn more on the Directed Studies website.

title: Beyond Morality: Nietzsche’s Non-Prescriptive Project
text:
Directed Studies, Historical and Political Thought, Prof. Christopher McGowan, Spring 2026
Argues that the Genealogy of Morals calls morality itself into question rather than prescribing master morality, reading Nietzsche’s perspectivism as a method that ends in productive uncertainty.

title: Questioning Hegel: Master-Slave Dialectic in Motion
text:
Directed Studies, Philosophy, Prof. Tamar Gendler, Spring 2026
Reconstructs Hegel’s account of self-consciousness through recognition and asks why the master-slave dialectic stops where it does, and whether the slave’s independence through labor contradicts it.

title: About Me
text:
I’m Camilo Salgar Duarte, a student at Yale College pursuing a double major in Applied Mathematics and Philosophy (Class of 2029). I grew up in Bogotá, Colombia.
My work sits where mathematical modeling meets philosophy. I’m drawn to questions in AI ethics, existential philosophy, and modernist literature, and to what happens when the tools we build start changing how we understand ourselves. I began at Yale in Directed Studies, and in summer 2026 I studied Mathematical Modelling and the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence at the University of Oxford’s Exeter College Summer Programme.
Outside the classroom, I grade for Yale’s Linear Algebra course, serve as Vice-President of Club Colombia at Yale, and sit on the board of the Yale College Chess Club. I’ve worked on FX and commodity hedging tools at Gestión de Riesgo and studied reinforcement learning at Quantil. I also play competitive chess and follow Independiente Santa Fe.
